Authored\n`defaults.toolPolicy` and non-empty `defaults.validity` gates are refused at\nhosted CLI launch (`TOOL_POLICY_UNSUPPORT
ED` / the corresponding validity\nrefusal). Hosted platform-authored suites do not currently have a backend\ntool-policy field or
enforcement path, so the CLI does not upload a suite that\nwould claim those guarantees. When supported by an eval runner, `toolPo
licy`\nis enforced at execution time with denied tools kept visible but blocked;\nserver annotations are advisory and **UNTRUSTED*
*. The file's default count\n(`defaults.repetitions`, or `defaults.iterations` in `schemaVersion: \"2\"`) is\ninherited per case a
nd is not uploaded as a suite `minIterations` floor.\nAuthored `defaults.systemPrompt` and `defaults.temperature` are uploaded as\
nexecution defaults; omitted fields stay omitted so the platform applies its\nown defaults. `target.hosts` and `target.environment
` are attached before\nlaunch. A file environment takes precedence over file hosts for that launch,\nwhile an explicit CLI target
takes precedence over both. When an explicit CLI\ntarget is provided (for example `--host`), the file's `target.hosts` are\n**not*
* synchronized to the suite's persisted host attachments — the suite\nkeeps whatever hosts it already has. Host attachment synchro
nization only\nruns when no explicit CLI target overrides the file. Environment attachment\nsynchronization is unaffected and alwa

ys runs.

Without `--idempotency-key`, the CLI mints a fresh UUID for every invocation
and prints it to stderr before launch (`
Eval idempotency key: <key>`). Each\ninvocation therefore starts and bills a new run. To retry a launch whose\nresponse was lost —
without starting a second run — pass the key that was\nprinted: `--idempotency-key <printed-key>`. A replay is marked `deduped` i

n
the receipt and human output. `--notes` is not part of the key.

##### Imported cases: live tool resolution, and per-run appr

oval

Every file run performs the same live check `eval validate --project` performs,
**before it writes anything**. It is not

opt-in and there is no flag to skip
it. A file with no deterministic `toolCall` steps asks no question and pays no
round trip.

What happens when a deterministic reference does not resolve depends on the
case:

| Case | Outcome |
| - | - |
| Selected
(enabled, and named by `--case` if you used it) | The launch **refuses before the suite is synced** — nothing is written and nothi
ng is billed |\n| Imported, not selected | Its claim is rewritten to `unresolved` (keeping `sourceCaseKey`) and it is **still pers
isted**, so the hosted record says what MCPJam found rather than still asserting a claim about a missing tool |\n| Native, not sel
ected | Left exactly as authored. A hand-written case never acquires an `import` block from this — \"somebody wrote this\" and \"s

omething converted this" are different facts |

Each target is checked on **its own** server set. `--host` is checked against
that host's configured servers rather than the file's, because that is the set\nthe run connects — validating `target.servers` wou
ld approve a tool the host\ncannot reach. A host the FILE declares uses its own `servers` list when it\ndeclares one (those are at
tached to the host before launch) and the host's\nconfigured set when the field is omitted. An explicitly empty `servers: []`\nis
a real, empty set — it clears the attachment before launch — and is\nvalidated as such, never as an omitted field. A step that pin
numerated before the suite exists\n(`--all-targets`, `--compose-*`), or a host does not report a server set, or a\nhost pins a ser

ver the project no longer has, the launch refuses rather than
assuming the references are fine.

`--case` accepts a hosted row
id, which does not exist yet when this check\nruns. A selector this stage cannot map is therefore treated as possibly naming\nany

enabled case, so an unresolved reference still refuses; the launcher
resolves the selector itself a moment later.

A selected `

approximated` case refuses unless this invocation approves it:

| Flag | Required | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--allow-app
roximated <case...>` | No | Approve an `approximated` imported case for **this run only**, by AUTHORED case id (`cases[].id`). Rep
eatable. `--file` runs only |\n| `--approval-reason <text>` | With the above | Why the approximations are acceptable for this run.
1–500 characters after trimming; one reason covers every approval in the invocation |\n\n```bash theme={\"theme\":\"css-variables
\"}\nmcpjam cloud eval run --file .mcpjam/evals/s_billing.yaml \\\n --allow-approximated c_refund_partial \\\n --approval-reason

"Reviewed against the upstream rubric; ENG-4821"
```

Checked before anything is billed, each with its own message: approvin
g a\n**native** case (nothing to approve), a **claimed-exact** one (needs no\napproval), an **unsupported** or **unresolved** one
(approval covers a case\nwhose behaviour was approximated, not one whose behaviour is missing), a\n**disabled** or **unselected**
one (the run will not execute it), an unknown\nid, or the same id twice. The flags are refused outright with `--suite`: a\nhosted

suite's cases are not the ones this invocation authored, so an
authored-id selector has nothing to resolve against.

**The appr
oval belongs to the run, never to the case.** You supply an id and a\nreason and nothing else — the approver and the timestamp are
derived by the\nserver and frozen into that run's own snapshot, because a caller-supplied\napprover would file one person's appro
val under another's name and a\ncaller-supplied timestamp could be backdated past the edit that invalidated the\nclaim. Nothing pe

rsists: edit the suite, re-sync, or launch again, and the flags
### `cloud eval run`

Start an eval run of an existing suite, o
r upload a versioned suite file and run it. Provide **either** `--suite` **or** `--file`, not both.\n\nBy default the command prin
ts a launch receipt and returns immediately. `--wait` polls every launched run to a terminal state.\n\n**Exit codes (`--wait` only
).** Without `--wait` this command's exit code is unchanged: `0` on any launch, `1` on a partial or wholly failed fan-out. `--wait
` owns a separate six-code contract — a caller who asked this process to sit and watch a run to completion is asking it to say how

the run went:

| Code | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `0` | Every waited run passed, unanimously, and (when a report was requested) e
very report was assembled |\n| `1` | A run **completed** with a **failed** verdict. The only condition that produces this code |\n
| `2` | Usage error — bad flags, `--reporter`/`--out` without `--wait`, or an invalid suite file (after auth, before any server/mo
del work) |\n| `3` | Auth failed — no credential, or the platform rejected it, at launch or mid-wait (a token that expired during
a long poll). Zero credits spent if it happened before launch |\n| `4` | Connection/setup failed before evaluation — a launch fail
ure this CLI itself observed (network, timeout, rate limit, a partial or failed fan-out, an unrecognized launch error), or a local
`--out` write failure — unless a more severe outcome (`1` or `3`) already applies to the same run, per the merge order above |\n|
`5` | No valid verdict — `inconclusive`, a null/unrecognized result, a run whose own status is failed/cancelled/timed-out, a wait
that hit its deadline, a mid-wait failure that was not auth-shaped, or a report that could not be assembled |\n\nNo infrastructur
e condition ever maps to `1` — see the same rule under `eval gate` below. A multi-target launch merges these worst-of across every
waited run, in the order `1 > 3 > 4 > 5 > 0`: a real verdict failure is never masked by a sibling's infrastructure noise, and a c
redential failure (which may be *why* other targets show no verdict) outranks a plain connection failure.\n\nThis six-code contrac
t is new and deliberately **different** from `eval gate`'s four codes below — see that command's own doc for why the two are not u
nified. An invalid suite file exits **2** either way — `eval validate` still exits 1 for the same contract failure, because it is

a verdict on the file and this command is not.

| Flag | Required | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--suite <id-or-name>` | Yes
